reason: E1 supports the creation of SCCPs and their role in maintaining ductility through coherent interfaces, but it does not address radiation tolerance or defect sink behaviour. E2 suggests that compositional complexity may improve He irradiation tolerance, but it does not mention nanoprecipitates as defect sinks. premises: Coherent nanoprecipitates in tungsten RHEAs can be introduced via stepwise controllable processing (SCCPs).
Coherent interfaces of such nanoprecipitates facilitate dislocation transmission and relieve stress concentrations, preserving ductility.
Coherent nanoprecipitates can act as efficient sinks for irradiation-induced defects (vacancies and interstitials).
Increasing compositional complexity in RHEAs may increase tolerance to He irradiation.
